name: Vienna Werkbund Estate
by: Josef Frank (plan) with about 30 architects incl. Loos, Rietveld, Neutra, Hoffmann
key_features: Model estate of 70 small houses by about 30 architects, among them Loos, Rietveld, Neutra and Hoffmann.

name: Stadio Flaminio
by: Pier Luigi Nervi and Antonio Nervi
key_features: The Nervis' stadium for the 1960 Rome Olympics; closed in 2011 and now decaying, with a conservation plan.

name: Lovell Health House
key_features: Often called the first steel-frame house in the US; its balconies hang from the roof frame on a hillside.

name: Miller House and Garden
by: Eero Saarinen; garden by Dan Kiley; interiors by Alexander Girard
key_features: Flat-roofed glass pavilion on a grid of cruciform columns, with a sunken conversation pit and Kiley garden.

name: Manufacturers Trust Company Building
by: Gordon Bunshaft and Charles Evans Hughes III (SOM)
key_features: Glass-walled bank on Fifth Avenue that shows its round steel vault door, by Henry Dreyfuss, to the street.

name: First Christian Church
key_features: Limestone-and-brick church with a 166 ft freestanding tower; among the first modernist churches in the US.

name: Villa Stein-de Monzie (Les Terrasses)
key_features: White box of strip windows set out with regulating lines; a canopy marks the door and a balcony the service entrance.

name: Oca, Ibirapuera Park
key_features: Low white concrete dome pierced by round windows, with curving ramps and floors inside.

name: Brasília TV Tower
key_features: Steel lattice mast on a concrete base with a viewing deck, set on Brasília's Monumental Axis.

name: Morumbi Stadium (Estádio Cícero Pompeu de Toledo)
key_features: Huge oval concrete bowl in three tiers, by the leader of São Paulo's brutalist school.

name: Teatro Cultura Artística
key_features: Concert hall whose curved street front carries Di Cavalcanti's huge glass-mosaic mural.

name: Brasília Bus Station (Rodoviária do Plano Piloto)
key_features: Multi-level concrete platform at the crossing of Brasília's two axes: buses below, roads over the top.

name: Palácio da Justiça (Ministry of Justice), Brasília
key_features: Glass box behind a row of concrete arches, with water pouring from chutes between them into a pool.

name: Torre Insignia (Banobras Tower)
key_features: 25-storey triangular prism at Tlatelolco, its apex crowned by a 47-bell carillon.

name: Covered Plaza, University City of Caracas
key_features: Covered plaza made as an open museum: perforated walls, gaps in the roof and ramps among murals and sculpture.

name: Parque Central Complex
key_features: Megastructure of tall concrete housing slabs and twin office towers, the tallest in Latin America until 2003.

name: Villa Planchart (Quinta El Cerrito)
key_features: Ponti's 'butterfly' villa on a hill over Caracas, with thin floating roofs and walls treated as sheets.

name: Estadio Centenario
key_features: Concrete bowl built for the first World Cup in 1930, with the Art Deco Tower of Homage over the main stand.

name: Ministry of Public Works Building
key_features: Art Deco office tower astride Avenida 9 de Julio, its two end faces now carrying steel portraits of Evita.

name: New York State Pavilion
key_features: Elliptical 'Tent of Tomorrow' with a cable-suspended roof on concrete columns, beside the observation towers.

name: No 1 Poultry
by: James Stirling, Michael Wilford and Associates
key_features: Wedge-shaped block in bands of pink and yellow stone, with a clock and turret on its sharp prow.

name: Mondadori Palace
key_features: Five-storey glass office block hung from concrete arches of differing widths, floating over a lake.

name: Ray and Maria Stata Center (MIT Building 32)
key_features: Leaning towers in brick, steel and coloured panels, crowded together like a small hill town.

name: Quartier Schützenstraße
key_features: One city block split into many narrow, brightly coloured facades around inner courtyards.

name: Hill of the Buddha
key_features: A 13.5 m Buddha ringed by a lavender-planted hill; only its head shows until you enter by a tunnel.

name: Zentrum Paul Klee
key_features: Three steel-ribbed waves rising out of the fields, for galleries, archive and a children's studio.

name: Hong Kong International Airport Terminal 1
key_features: Vast terminal under a repeated run of light steel barrel-vaulted roof shells that let daylight in.

name: Milstein Hall, Cornell University
key_features: Long glass studio floor that cantilevers over the street, linking two old architecture buildings.

name: Pierresvives
key_features: Long horizontal 'tree trunk' of concrete and glass holding the archives, library and sports offices.

name: European Court of Human Rights Building
by: Richard Rogers Partnership with Claude Bucher
key_features: Two drum-shaped courtrooms at the head of a long office 'tail', on the bank of the river Ill.

name: Lucerne Culture and Congress Centre (KKL)
key_features: A thin 100 m square roof cantilevers far out over the lakeside, sheltering concert hall, museum and congress halls.

name: Tanzbrunnen (Star Wave Tent)
key_features: Star-shaped fabric membrane pulled up on masts, floating over a dance floor in a fountain basin.

name: Nara Centennial Hall
key_features: Long hall with curved, dark-tiled walls like a ship's hull, beside Nara station.

name: Opera Village (Operndorf Afrika)
key_features: Village of school, health centre and houses on a laterite plateau, begun in 2010 with Christoph Schlingensief.

name: West Village (Basis Yard)
key_features: Five-storey building ringing a whole city block around sports pitches, with a ramp up to the roof.

name: The Circle, Zurich Airport
key_features: A small city of glass-walled blocks and lanes curving along the hill beside the airport terminal.

name: Emerson College Los Angeles
key_features: Ten-storey frame of two slim residential slabs and a bridge, wrapping a sculpted block of classrooms.

name: Vulcania
key_features: Mostly underground museum marked by a split cone clad in dark volcanic stone and lined with gold.

name: Preston Bus Station
by: Building Design Partnership (Keith Ingham, Charles Wilson) with Ove Arup & Partners
key_features: Bus station under a five-storey car park whose curved concrete balconies run the full length; Grade II.

name: Kingsgate Bridge
key_features: Concrete footbridge on V-shaped legs, built as two halves along the banks and swung 90° to meet; Grade I.

name: Media-TIC
key_features: Steel-framed cube wrapped in inflatable ETFE cushions that shade the offices from the sun.

name: LocHal
by: Civic Architects, Braaksma & Roos, Inside Outside (Petra Blaisse)
key_features: 1932 locomotive shed turned public library; huge movable textile screens divide the vast hall.

name: Unilever-Haus
key_features: Offices around a tall open atrium, wrapped in a loose ETFE foil skin against the harbour wind.

name: Quay Quarter Tower
key_features: A 1970s office tower kept and grown: its core reused, wrapped in five shifted, stacked glass boxes.

name: Max Aicher Arena
key_features: Hall about 200 m by 90 m with no inner columns, roofing over the old outdoor speed-skating oval.

name: Kurilpa Bridge
key_features: Tensegrity footbridge: masts and cables at scattered angles hold the deck and its small shade canopies.

name: Surat Diamond Bourse
key_features: Nine 15-storey office towers joined by a central spine, with landscaped courts between them.

name: Qatar Faculty of Islamic Studies
key_features: Faculty and mosque raised on columns, marked by two tall white minarets carved with calligraphy.

name: Museum of Memory and Tolerance
key_features: Seven-level concrete and steel museum facing the Alameda, wrapped round an atrium with a floating Children's Memorial.

name: Scale Lane Bridge
key_features: Swing footbridge that people can stay on while it pivots to let boats pass; its drum sits on the bank.

name: Sara Kulturhus
key_features: Culture centre and 20-storey hotel tower built in timber; the hotel is stacked prefabricated CLT room modules.

name: Paula Fox Melanoma and Cancer Centre
key_features: Six-storey cancer centre on St Kilda Road, wrapped in a light-filtering facade veil modelled on healthy skin.

name: Wyndham Court
by: Lyons Israel Ellis (E. D. Lyons, Frank Linden, Aubrey Hume)
key_features: 184 flats over shops in white board-marked concrete, six to seven storeys on a slope, with tall stair towers.

name: University of East Anglia Ziggurats (Norfolk and Suffolk Terraces)
key_features: Stepped student residences rising like ziggurats from the meadow above the lake, linked to Lasdun's teaching wall.

name: J. Edgar Hoover Building
by: C. F. Murphy and Associates (Stanislaw Z. Gladych)
key_features: FBI headquarters in buff precast concrete: 11 storeys on E Street, 8 on Pennsylvania Avenue, round a trapezoid court.

name: Temple Street Parking Garage
key_features: Long concrete car park for 1,280 cars on arched double columns, bridging George Street, with shops below.

name: Wurster Hall
by: Joseph Esherick, Vernon DeMars, Donald Olsen
key_features: Berkeley's architecture school: a raw concrete tower and wings round a courtyard, hung with 592 sunshades.

name: Institute of Hygiene and Microbiology
key_features: Sculptural concrete research and teaching building, listed as a key work of organic and brutalist post-war modernism.

name: St. Agnes (König Galerie)
by: Werner Düttmann; conversion by Arno Brandlhuber
key_features: Former church of rough-textured blocks with a square bell tower; converted into an art gallery in 2015.

name: Eastern City Gate (Rudo)
key_features: Three 28-storey, 85 m housing towers with stepped, tapering profiles, marking the road into Belgrade from the east.

name: Ruhr University Bochum
key_features: Campus of 14 near-identical slab blocks, meant as ships in a 'harbour of knowledge', linked by concrete decks.

name: Goce Delčev Student Dormitory
key_features: Exposed-concrete student towers with projecting service shafts and sky bridges, built in two phases.

name: TASS Building
key_features: News-agency headquarters with deep, round-cornered window frames in sandstone and a globe over the entrance.

name: Queensland Art Gallery
key_features: Low, light-coloured concrete gallery organised along an indoor Watermall, with planted terraces by the river.

name: Golden Mile Complex
by: Design Partnership (Gan Eng Oon, William Lim, Tay Kheng Soon)
key_features: 16-storey mixed-use block with a stepped, terraced section: flats over a shopping podium, facing the sea.

name: Joseph Regenstein Library
key_features: Library of grooved limestone in stacked vertical fins that read like concrete, on the site of Stagg Field.

name: Scarborough College (Andrews Building)
key_features: Two wings meet at a central atrium; wide indoor 'streets' with balconies keep students out of the winter.

name: Miami Marine Stadium
key_features: Concrete grandstand for 6,566 under a cantilevered folded-plate roof on eight slanted columns, facing a boat basin.

name: Slovak National Gallery Extension
by: Vladimír Dedeček; renovation by Architekti BKPŠ
key_features: Long gallery wing lifted on piers like a bridge (the 'Overbridge') in front of the older gallery buildings.

name: University Hall, University of Lethbridge
key_features: 912 ft, nine-storey concrete block laid along the coulees above the Oldman River like the nearby rail viaduct.

name: National Arts Centre
key_features: Performing-arts centre in reinforced concrete, planned on interlocking hexagons and triangles beside the Rideau Canal.

name: Majdanek Mausoleum
key_features: 35 m concrete dome raised on three supports over a bowl of victims' ashes, at the end of a 1.3 km memorial road.

name: Kirishima International Concert Hall (Miyama Conseru)
key_features: Shoebox hall bent into a leaf-shaped plan with a keel-like section for sound, set in open hill country.

name: National Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto
key_features: Granite and glass facade ruled by a 1.5 m grid, with glazed corner stair towers, facing Okazaki Park.

name: Shanghai Suhe MixC World
key_features: Shopping centre under a park on Suzhou Creek: planted slopes step down into an "urban valley" to the shops.

name: London Bridge Station
key_features: Rebuilt station with a huge street-level concourse under the tracks and long curved canopies over the platforms.

name: Lanserhof Sylt
key_features: Health resort under Europe's largest thatched roof; ridge and eaves swing with the dunes, loggias cut into the thatch.

name: Nissay Theatre (Nippon Life Hibiya Building)
key_features: Stone-clad block facing Hibiya Park; inside, a hall with no straight lines and 20,000 pearl shells overhead.

name: Kadokawa Culture Museum
key_features: Angular polyhedron clad in 20,000 granite plates, as if rock had broken up through the ground; 8 m bookshelf theatre.

name: National Museum of Japanese History
key_features: Long, low national history museum on the former grounds of Sakura Castle, where the old moat survives.

name: Shinjuku Park Tower
key_features: Three linked towers of 52, 47 and 41 storeys stepping down in height, each topped by a glazed pyramid.

name: Embassy of Kuwait, Tokyo
key_features: Block-like concrete volumes stacked asymmetrically round a raised courtyard: chancery below, residence above.

name: Komazawa Olympic Park Control Tower and Gymnasium
key_features: A 50 m concrete tower of stacked slab tiers, a modern pagoda, rising from a raised plaza beside the gymnasium.

name: Toyota Stadium
key_features: Curved roofs hung by cables from four giant masts, so no columns block the view; massive concrete piers below.

name: NOA Building
key_features: A near-windowless dark oval tower rising from a low red-brick drum: 15 storeys of office.

name: Takanawa Gateway Station
key_features: Folded, origami-like roof of steel and laminated timber under a translucent membrane, like shoji screens.

name: Kasumigaseki Building
key_features: Japan's first modern skyscraper, 36 floors on a flexible steel frame built to ride out earthquakes.

name: Nippon Budokan
key_features: Octagonal hall modelled on the Yumedono of Horyu-ji, its sweeping roof meant to recall Mount Fuji, topped by a giboshi.

name: Kyoto Tower
key_features: A white candle of welded steel rings and plate, no lattice, standing on a nine-storey hotel block by Kyoto Station.

name: Mt. Fuji World Heritage Centre, Shizuoka
key_features: Inverted cone of hinoki timber lattice over a pool, whose reflection completes the shape of Mount Fuji.

name: The Prince Kyoto Takaragaike (Kyoto Takaragaike Prince Hotel)
key_features: Ring-shaped hotel: 310 rooms along one corridor round a garden court, the rounded tiers stepping back.

name: Academic Bookstore (Kirjatalo)
key_features: Copper-clad bookshop whose three-storey hall is lit by crystal-like prismatic skylights.

name: Filmhuset
key_features: Exposed-concrete film house shaped like a camera, its cast walls patterned like film strips.

name: Henie Onstad Kunstsenter
key_features: Low concrete art centre stepping over a wooded headland on the Oslofjord.

name: Sanomatalo
key_features: Helsinki's first all-glass building: a newspaper house with public commercial floors at street level.

name: Sibelius Hall
key_features: Glulam timber concert hall in a glass box, joined to an old brick factory on the shore of Lake Vesijärvi.

name: Stockholm City Hall
key_features: Dark-red brick palace on the water with a 106 m tower, open courtyard and arcade to the lake.

name: Helsinki Olympic Stadium
key_features: White functionalist stadium with a 72.71 m tower, the length of the 1932 Olympic javelin win.

name: Helsingborg Concert Hall
key_features: Classic Swedish functionalism: a tall white hall box fronted by a low curved foyer wing.

name: Sveriges Riksbank Building
key_features: Dark stone block of squares and cubes on Brunkebergstorg, composed to look solid and stable.
